cognitive_classification.crux_move: In horizontal strip [2][5][3][6], alternate faces fold into mutually parallel opposite faces: Face 5 is opposite Face 6

source_question.stem: Which of the following numbers lies on the face opposite to the face having number 5, when the given net is folded to form a cube?

answer.crux_move_ref: In horizontal strip [2][5][3][6], alternate faces fold into mutually parallel opposite faces: Face 5 is opposite Face 6

hint_ladder.hint1_conceptual_nudge: In a planar cube net, faces separated by exactly one square along a straight row become opposite parallel faces when folded into 3D.
hint_ladder.hint2_tactical_step: Identify which face is separated from 5 by exactly one square along the horizontal 4-square strip [2][5][3][6].

solution.derivation: In a 4-square strip of a cube net, alternate faces are opposite in the assembled 3D cube. In [2][5][3][6], Face 2 is opposite Face 3, and Face 5 is opposite Face 6. Therefore, the face opposite 5 is 6 (Option A).

independent_check.verification: Fold along boundaries: Face 5 forms base, Face 3 right side, Face 6 ceiling directly opposite Face 5. Option A uniquely verified.

distractor_analysis.B: Face 1 folds opposite to Face 4 on the vertical flaps.
distractor_analysis.C: Face 4 is adjacent to Face 5 along the upper shared edge.
distractor_analysis.D: Face 2 is opposite Face 3 in the horizontal strip.

html_representation:
D1 REPRESENT Unit: Cube Nets

Which of the following numbers lies on the face opposite to the face having number 5, when the given net is folded to form a cube?

In a planar cube net, faces separated by exactly one square along a straight row become opposite parallel faces when folded into 3D.

Identify which face is separated from 5 by exactly one square along the horizontal 4-square strip [2][5][3][6].

Show Complete Solution

In a 4-square strip of a cube net, alternate faces are opposite in the assembled 3D cube. In [2][5][3][6], Face 2 is opposite Face 3, and Face 5 is opposite Face 6. Therefore, the face opposite 5 is 6 (Option A).
